title: Vijay's Final Film Jana Nayagan Hits Theaters With Record Advance Bookings
excerpt: The political thriller marks Thalapathy Vijay's farewell to cinema as he transitions to full-time politics, with trade analysts projecting a ₹90-100 crore worldwide opening day.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jana Nayagan is Vijay's 69th and final film, released on July 23 after a six-month delay.
  • The film achieved over 1 million advance ticket bookings, only the fifth Tamil film to do so.
  • Analysts project ₹90-100 crore worldwide opening day, with ₹250 crore estimated for the weekend.
  • Directed by H. Vinoth, the film has a reported budget of ₹500 crore and features Pooja Hegde.

Tamil superstar Vijay's much-anticipated final film Jana Nayagan arrived in theaters on Wednesday amid celebrations across Tamil Nadu and packed screenings in diaspora markets worldwide. The political thriller, which was delayed six months over disputes with India's Central Board of Film Certification, marks Vijay's formal farewell to a three-decade acting career as he focuses on his role as a political leader.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=iTuvRLLsXVE

"In India, I estimate an opening of ₹60 crore. Globally, my estimate is ₹90 crore."

— Ramesh Bala, trade analyst

Record-Breaking Advance Sales

The film crossed the 1 million ticket milestone on BookMyShow in advance bookings, making it only the fifth Tamil film in history to achieve the feat. For Vijay, it marks a hat-trick — he now has three films in the elite club alongside Leo and The Greatest of All Time (GOAT), surpassing Rajinikanth, who holds two entries with Jailer and Coolie.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2080131920038678730

By the eve of release, the film had accumulated approximately ₹20 crore in advance bookings domestically and ₹33 crore worldwide, with around 731,000 tickets sold on BookMyShow alone. Nearly 10,000 shows were scheduled across India, with over 3,500 in Tamil Nadu — though trade observers noted the bookings grew steadily rather than the explosive sellouts some had expected for a farewell film of this magnitude.

A Politically Charged Title Card

Early audiences flagged a striking moment in the film's first half: a title card that lists Vijay's name with three successive epithets — Ilaya Thalapathy Vijay, Thalapathy Vijay, and the Honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. The sequence, which traces the evolution of his public identity from young actor to political leader, sent social media into a frenzy.

Vijay, who launched his political party Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and subsequently became Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister, has positioned Jana Nayagan — meaning "People's Leader" — as his cinematic farewell before devoting himself to governance full-time.

Vijay's Biggest Grosser: Leo

The Box-Office Question

Directed by H. Vinoth and produced by KVN Productions on a reported budget of ₹500 crore, the film features an ensemble cast including Pooja Hegde, Bobby Deol, and Mamitha Baiju, with music by Anirudh Ravichander. Trade expert Ramesh Bala projects an opening weekend of ₹150-180 crore in India and ₹250 crore worldwide.

The central benchmark is Leo, Vijay's biggest grosser at an estimated ₹606 crore worldwide, followed by GOAT at roughly ₹458 crore. Whether Jana Nayagan can surpass those numbers will depend heavily on overseas collections, where Vijay has built one of Indian cinema's strongest fan bases among diaspora audiences.

Why the Diaspora Is Watching

For Tamil communities abroad — particularly in Southeast Asia, the Gulf states, the United States, and the United Kingdom — Jana Nayagan carries emotional weight beyond box-office arithmetic. It represents the final performance of a star who has been a cultural touchstone for over 30 years. Overseas pre-sales stood at ₹15 crore ahead of release, and early morning screenings in multiple time zones drew capacity crowds.

The film's journey to theaters was itself dramatic. Originally slated for a Pongal (January) release, it was held up by the censor board and suffered an online leak. Despite these setbacks, the advance booking trajectory suggests the Thalapathy brand remains resilient — and that Indian cinema audiences are ready to give Vijay a blockbuster farewell.
